  Barber, Khione95, Nexus 837; its author allows compatibility, not bundling). "Heroine of Pywell": not found by a

  "Short version: we don't sync looks ourselves, the game does. In the shared-world builds both players are in the
  host's game world, and each player's character is the game's own player character, loaded from that player's own
  save. The game tells the other PC what you wear and what your save says about your look, and the other PC draws it
  with its own game files. We never send models or mod files. So for any appearance mod the question is 'does my
  friend's PC have the same data', not whether it uses an .asi. Character Creator: it keeps your look in the save as
  picks from the barber's lists and fills those lists with its own faces and hair, so a friend without the identical
  mod has nothing at those entries. With the same version on both PCs it may well work; we have not tested it, which
  is why it is listed as unsupported. We can't ship it either: its author is fine with compatibility, not with
  bundling. Heroine of Pywell: not tested and I haven't looked inside it. If it replaces Kliff's model files, each
  PC shows what its own files say: you see the heroine (most likely on your friend's Kliff too) and a friend without
  it sees plain Kliff; if both install it, both see it. A mod that changes the character only through its own code
  while the game runs shows on your PC only, unless both run it. If you try either with a friend, a screenshot from
  both sides in #play-testing-feedback would help a lot."

## T02 -- Anti-cheat and terms check
Plan: research the game's DRM / anti-cheat / online services; list the in-process vs online pieces; add a start-up
guard (anti-cheat modules in the process, anti-cheat files in the game folder) that keeps every part of Co-op+ off;
dev switch to simulate a hit; README + findings note.
Done: no anti-cheat (Denuvo Anti-Tamper = DRM); server is in-process; online pieces = Steam, Denuvo licence,
cross-save (PA account), sentry/kafka. src/mod/online_guard.* ; guard tripped (dev online_guard_test=winmm.dll):
log 8 lines, nothing installed, message box shown; normal start: "co-op allowed", all hooks as before.
docs/research/online-integrity.md, README "IS IT SAFE?". Note: when tripped the overlay is not installed either, so
the message is a plain Windows box (an anti-cheat could flag the DXGI hook).

## T03 -- Version handshake
Plan: Hello / Welcome carry the game's exe version (protocol 10 -> 11; the reader rejects trailing bytes, so a bump);
ClientSession refuses another mod build or game version on both sides (no Connected, so no spawn / events), with a

own Wait is overridden by the host's time, which is the defined rule (time follows the host).

## T48 -- 3-4 player support: not started (deferred)
The architecture is two-player throughout: ClientSession has one peer, the puppet is one copy (kPuppetBody /
kPuppetHorse keys), the enemy relay keys copies by "the partner", challenges and revive assume one other player,
the party frame shows one friend. Scaling already has 3-4 player curves (scaling.toml). Doing it without destabilising
2-player play means a session per peer and N puppets (new reserved actor keys) -- a project of its own; the roadmap
allows skipping it ("only if the architecture allows it").

## Quest sync (user priority 2026-11-03 ~21:30, asked for by a Discord player)
- Live sync stays impossible: each player's in-process server ignores outside quest requests (D42).
- Offline route investigated: quest progress is one save object, QuestSaveData (stage / mission / quest / quest-gauge
  state lists, last completed main quest; ~1.8 MB, ~50 000 elements). Missions appear in the list as the story
  unlocks them (slot101: 3201 entries / 221 done; slot0: 3475 / 477), so it cannot be an in-place byte patch.
- tools/save/quest_sync.py: transplant(base, donor, object): copies an object between saves, renumbers its elements'
  type indices to the target schema (each save carries its own schema; missing types appended), rebases self
  pointers, splices it in (splice.py) and checks the result (all other objects byte-identical, the moved object
  element-for-element the donor's, encode round trip).
- In game (build/port3479/qsync_test.sh; "Party journal: N missions known, M done" logged at login; test copies of the
  user's saves in slot103 only, removed after; savecheck OK every round):
  * slot0 + slot2's quests (same schema): loads, 2485 known / 456 done. Mechanism works.
  * slot101 + slot0's quests, slot0 + bandit save's quests, bandit save + slot0's character objects, and even the
    40-byte CharacterStatusSaveData alone: all crash at load (exe+0x1563971 -> call 0x0). Identity re-encodes load.
  * Cause: the saves were written by different game versions: the user's slots are the 2026-11-01 backups (older
    build; the game migrates them at load), the bandit save was written by 1.0.0.3479 and its types have more fields
    (FieldNPCSaveData _affinityList, ItemSaveData _averagePrice, QuestSaveData, QuestGaugeStateData...). A block
    written under one field list is unreadable under another.
- Status: works for two saves of the same game version (what co-op partners have); NOT verified for a big story gap,
  because no two same-version saves at different story points exist here and making one needs an in-game save.
  Also open: whether quests alone are enough or the world objects that follow the story (FieldSaveData,
  NPCScheduleStageManagerSaveData, FactionSaveData, KnowledgeSaveData, FogSaveData...) must come along.
- "Continue" picks the slot by the time in its lobby.save: test variants need the bandit save's lobby.save.
- 2026-11-03 ~23:10 FOUND the load crash (exe+0x1563971 -> call 0x0): not the game version. Self pointers come after an
  8-byte run that is FF x 8 everywhere EXCEPT in FactionSpawnStageManagerSaveData, whose elements carry their index
  there (0, 1, 2, ...; 158 in slot101, 170 in slot0). Our tools only knew FF runs, so any change that moved those
  elements (a size change before them: a type added to the schema, a resized object) left their pointers stale, and
  the faction-spawn loader read garbage. Proof chain (all slot103 test copies): one unused type appended -> crash;
  same with a different type, either save -> crash; two types swapped and renumbered (no size change) -> loads;
  header float at 0x08 zeroed -> still crash; plain re-encode -> loads. splice.self_pointers now finds every u32 equal
  to its own position + 4, whatever the 8 bytes before it (slower, ~4 s a save). Also fixed: the blob size stored at

    "Create Address Tables" is off for data slices. Deep mode's WindowsResourceReference looped forever: off.
  - RTTI found nothing at first. Cause: this exe's section names are not the usual ones. Ghidra's RttiAnalyzer looks
    for TypeDescriptors in ".data*" and the type_info vftable in ".rdata*"; here `.rodata` (RVA 0x6CD2000) is really
    the writable data with the TypeDescriptors and `.arch` (0x5597000) is really the read-only data with the
    vftables. Also the analyzer skips itself once the "RTTI Found" program option exists. Fix:
    build/tools/scripts/RttiFix.java renames the blocks by RVA (.rodata -> .data, .sdata -> .data_s, .arch -> .rdata),
    removes "RTTI Found", runs RttiAnalyzer again (326 s): 15,068 vftables. RecoverClassesFromRTTIScript also refuses a
    program not marked analysed (GhidraProgramUtilities.markProgramAnalyzed).

## Bug reports 2026-11-07 (user: "Frame drops seem to be a rather big issue now")
Reports kept in build/reports/ (not in git): borque-2026-11-07_13-28-50 (Borque's CoopPlus report: build 096D9C3F,
Steam, Hernand plains) and plitos-C606D401-FPS-Test (Plitos' "C606D401 | FPS fix" test build on c606602d: a
200 KB patch with many features; its FPS parts: packet replay 16 packets / 2 ms per real packet, the enemy relay's
watch_hidden() scan only with diagnostics, enemy retries every 33 ms, DX12 overlay skips its draw instead of waiting).
- Borque, FPS from the overlay's present counter (presents per 5 s): ~90 fps solo; the session starts 13:10:34 and
  by 13:11:34 the game runs 27 fps, ~25 for minutes, 3-4 fps 13:24-13:26, 55 after. Our network loop at the same
  time: normally ~1000 loops / 10 s (6 ms waiting for input, 3 ms work); from 13:11:30 ~30 loops / 10 s, 300-450 ms
  of work each, "waiting for input" 0 -- busy all the time. Its sections grew together: coop-update 0 -> ~180 ms,
  state (local.sample + HUD) 0 -> ~60 ms, activity 3 -> ~40 ms; already while our own player was still loading (no
  copies yet). Borque's "+150 latency" is this: rtt 300+ ms because the loop runs every ~330 ms.
- Lead: every game::safe_read calls VirtualQuery (231 call sites). VirtualQuery takes the process's address-space
  lock that every VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree of the game's threads takes too; while the game streams the world, our
  reads and its allocations wait on each other (slowmo.cpp's note: one VirtualQuery per packet made a load arrive
  ~50 s late). A loop that reads more each second makes the game's frames wait more: both sides slow.
- Borque's crash: exe+0xA12E4E reading 0x115 again (thread 20044), with the action-events guard installed and working
  (5500+ waits). 1.4 s after the enemy copy 0xB01F0008 was reloaded "with no action": a race -- the guard's check and
  the game's read are on different moments; a copy reload in between leaves the action null.
- 2026-11-07 14:15-14:35 FPS FIX built and measured (two copies, bandits save, same settings as hz1; Ghidra's class
  recovery running in both measured runs):
  1. game::safe_read (safe_memory.cpp): no VirtualQuery per read any more -- a per-thread cache of 32 ranges already
     found committed + readable (1 s life); the copy stays under __try (a range freed since: caught, forgotten); a
     guard page met anyway gets its guard back. New line every 10 s: "Timing: guarded reads, 10 s: N from the range
     cache, M VirtualQuery calls, K faulted". fps1: ~1,000,000 reads per 10 s from the cache, ~3,200 VirtualQuery,
     0 faults (the old build made ~1,000,000 VirtualQuery calls per 10 s, many on the game's own animation threads:
     the HorseDiag guards read the CC of every character every frame).
  2. Enemy relay: watch_hidden() (a test aid: two actor lookups per known enemy every 2 s, log only) runs only with
     [dev] enemy_relay (as Plitos' C606D401 did).
  3. Crash guard: exe+0xA12E4E (Borque's crash) is in exe+0xA12C00, called by the CC tick 0x9451E0 -- NOT in
     0xA128C0 where the earlier guard sits (the full index showed it). copy_tick_would_fault() mirrors the game's own

- 2026-11-10 00:30 USER BUG REPORT on the playtest build (0.1.0-alpha+377f2c97, their real install): "Invite Friends"
  opens Steam's dialog but no friend can be invited, and the dialog's X does not close it (only Shift+Tab does).
  Their coopplus.log: 13 "Co-op lobby: Invite Friends" presses about 1 s apart, each re-opening the dialog.
  Two causes, both ours (layer, coop_page.cpp):
  1. mouse_hook (WH_MOUSE_LL) swallows every mouse button while the title lobby page is shown and queues it for our
     page. With Steam's overlay on top, the click never reached Steam AND pressed our card underneath again.
  2. game_input_block (GetForegroundWindow / GetActiveWindow return null to the game while our page is up) also
     starves Steam's overlay: it takes its clicks from the input the game reads. Hover still lit the X; clicks did not.
  Fix: steam_join.cpp registers a GameOverlayActivated_t (331) callback -> net::join_overlay_active(); while the
  overlay is open the mouse hook and coop_page_hook_key pass everything through, the page drops queued clicks / keys /
  pad presses, and the game input block is lifted. Log lines: "Join: the Steam overlay is open (its mouse and keys
  are Steam's)" / "... is closed".

  user install restored 5/5.

## 2026-11-10 tcB281 / tcB282: the trade worker's key checks pass; a USER key as receiver kills the host

- tcB281: same lost first press; nothing new. tcB282 (guest script before the host keys): the host died in the
  guest script's second call, so the host keys (quick message, glyph bisect) never ran. Both moved to tcB283, which
  runs without the trade script. Saves OK, install restored 5/5.
- Worker 0x2E0B2B0, read in the decomp: item key -> index (thunk exe+0x3D7E10, 0xFFFF = unknown) and inventory key
  -> index (thunk exe+0x3D5930) come first, either unknown = err exe+0x712DFEC. Then both actors by key
  (ServerActorManager vfunction5), a missing one = exe+0x712E058. Then the entry: row `entry` of the inventory's
  item-move table (0xA0 bytes each); type 3 or an empty source / target = 0x712DFEC again. Then the entry's
  condition, the distance check 0x2301D20 (reads both actors' +0x68 -> +0x20 and +0x1A0: they must be CHARACTERS),
  then type 2 -> 0x2DF2560, else the move 0x2DF04A0.
- Probe results (host, 3576): the inventory KEY is the plain inventory number: keys 0x1..0x15 -> index 0..20
  (0xDFE0 from dumpitemmove's "key?" was garbage). Item 22007 (0x55F7) -> index 0x5D7.
  * `trade3111 55F7 1 0 1 0` (receiver 0 = the giver, inventory 1, entry 0): passes every check, enters the move
    0x2DF04A0 (kind 1), which returns err 0xED0EF13C. The probe now also says where that constant lives in
    exe+0x7120000..0x7160000 so the decomp can name it.
  * `trade3111 55F7 1 90100000 1 0`: the log ends at "[worker in]" = the host process died there. 0x90100000 is the
    host's USER actor (0x90100065 = the guest's user, 0xA0100001 = the host's character, 0xA0100066 = the guest's
    character); the distance check dereferences character parts a user actor does not have. NEVER pass a user key.
    For the real feature the layer must validate the receiver is a character before it sends anything.
- Next (tcB284): receiver 0xA0100001, inventory 1, entry 3 (the kind 2 rows 3-7, bag -> 8, the 0x2DF2560 path).

### Trade route found in the decomp (2026-11-10, read only; not yet built)
3111 is closed (fixed routes), so a player-to-player give is built from two of the game's own server workers:
- **Add**: `exe+0x2DD8FC0 (holder, int* err, TrItemValue* v)`: the worker under CreateItemFromTrItemValueCheatReq
  (handler exe+0x2C8B130 -> exe+0x2EE96F0, which checks a cheat permission first, err exe+0x714BC48; calling the
  worker directly skips that). TrItemValue is 0x1C0 bytes, built by exe+0x2641950: +0 uid (-1), +8 u32 item key
  (not 0), +0xC u16 (0), +0x10 i64 count (>= 1), +0x5E u8 level.
- **Remove**: discard worker `exe+0x2E03330 (holder, int* err, actor, u16 inventory key, i16 slot, i64 count,
  transform*)` under DiscardItemReq (handler exe+0x2C8DE80). Errors: 0x714BFA0 empty slot, 0x714BFB4 not enough.
  Two paths by the item's row (+0x52): -1 = plain delete (the item-change transaction, reason 0x2F), position
  ignored; otherwise the item is DROPPED into the world at transform+0xC0 (zero position -> err 0x714B154).
- Holder = `exe+0x22F1DC0 (actor)` = `*(*(actor+0x68)+0xB8)` (0 when not a playable character). Holder +8 actor,
  +0x18 inventory array, +0x20 count; `exe+0x22F7FE0 (holder, inv idx, slot)` -> entry (+0 uid, +8 item idx,
  +0x10 count).
- Both use the server thread's TLS, so they must run on the server thread: inside our 3111 worker detour, set off by
  a magic `entry` value from the guest (the host checks that the receiver is a character and near).
- Not usable: DeleteItemCheat worker (clears a whole inventory), AddMinusItem worker (did nothing for bag items).

### RB glyph: the layout lever (2026-11-10, decomp read by an agent; not yet tested)
The menu root (vftable exe+0x5A033D0 = `UIGamePlayControl_Root_MainMenu`) has no "place RB" function: the glyph is
laid out by the game's CSS-like engine. The lever is the style length setter `exe+0x712F00 (styleHandle, u8* propId,
float* value, u8* unit, 0)` with `styleHandle = *(*(*(root+0x178)+8)+0x20)`; property ids: 2 Left, 0x15 MarginLeft,
0x4A TranslateX, 0xC Display, 0xD Visibility (byte setter exe+0x6D9090); unit 1 = scaled pixels, 2 = percent. It
invalidates the layout itself. To try: TranslateX on RB (UI thread), re-applied if the key guide refresh
(exe+0xE446C0) resets it. Root +0x1A8 = the tab controller (exe+0xF1CB50: LB -> previous, RB -> next).

### 2026-11-10 playtest report (Borque, host, two PCs over Steam relay, 0.1.0-alpha+22e8f365)

Report: build/playtest-reports/borque-2026-11-10_22-24-58 (local). Said: the guest got stuck in a loop at the Hernand
blacksmith, then every NPC vanished for the host; enemies did not seem to react to the guest's attacks; huge desyncs
arriving at Hernand.
- Cause of the vanishing and the desync: the host's tunnel to the guest. Its output was ~100 KB/s in the field,
  340-570 KB/s arriving at Hernand (a town's NPCs); the Steam relay ("relay 100") carried ~70 KB/s, so the backlog went
  0 -> 16 MB in 45 s (rtt 1.5 s, net loops of ~2 s), hit the 16 MB cap at 22:21:02, the link broke, user 2 was logged
  out (so the host saw the guest's world go) and nothing more crossed.
- The tunnel's batch compression (ByJunter's, measured x9.5 on a town burst) was OFF: tunnel_compress defaults to 0
  and the package never wrote it. Now native_mode_text writes tunnel_compress=1 for host and guest (layer test).
- Native safety valve (troc_frame TunnelSender): above 2 MB of backlog only the newest MoveActorAck 3094 per actor is
  kept (a stale position of the same actor is useless once a newer one waits); every other packet stays, in order;
  checked again every +512 KB and before a push would be refused. Status line: "congestion: N stale move(s) shed".
  Unit test test_tunnel_sender_shed passes (the optd suite's 11 older failures are the 2661 scene-parser tests,
  unrelated).
- "Enemies do not react to the guest": AntiGrief dropped 10 guest hits on NPC 0xB0100520 (22:18:16-22) and one on
  0xB0100351: an NPC with a dialog list counted as a protected person even when hostile. Now an NPC the HOST attacks
  (its own DoFrameEventReq) is no longer protected ("AntiGrief: NPC ... is no longer protected: the host fights it"),
  and a guest swing on enemies and townsfolk at once keeps the enemies (built earlier today).
- The blacksmith loop: the smithy scene was prepared at 22:20:18, right inside the 2 s network stalls; likely the same
  lag. Watch for it after the compression fix.
- Lootr probe (tcB311/tcB312): the hold on X did an interaction 0xF4263 on a nearby gimmick (3008 -> 2120, 3073 ->
  2794) but no pickup (no item added): not a Take. Probing parked behind the playtest fixes.

  install (builds 55722584 to 21f0f6d0) it stayed for good, at the title and in the world, with "?" where the keys
  were, and the first-run controls card waited behind it for ever. This is Borque's "inputs of the mod are not
  didplayed now" and "what should we select in the co-op menu to disable that text in the middle". Our harness wrote
  experimental_asked=1 into its test ini, so no test ever showed it. (The prologue line fixed in 21f0f6d0 was a real
  leftover too, but not what he saw.)

  first-time players through the whole flow: "experimental co-op saves + live quests off" (no "asking"), the
  first-run card "Seamless Co-op+: Invite and join friends from the title screen's Co-op menu / Hold (A) on your
  friend ... / Menu > Co-op ..." shows once (60 s or until a menu opens), nothing else on screen. SAVES OK.

  click it got. "Start Solo" is selected by default and sits in the middle of the screen, the game's own input is

### tcB405-tcB411 (2026-11-11 08:12-08:40): NO CO-OP MENU = frame generation; fixed

- D3vils (#play-testing-feedback 08:15-08:18): "its Xess Frame Generation the moment i turned it off the text
  appeared" (his settings: Intel XeSS 3.0, Native AA, Intel XeSS Frame Generation, 2 frames). So the missing title
  menu on the testers' PCs was not the DLC: with XeSS (and very likely AMD FSR) frame generation the game presents
  through that library's own swap chain class, not through Streamline's, whose Present we hook.
- Reproduced (tcB406, new harness switches -FrameGen -FrameGenMode Intel_XeSS_Frame_Generation -Upscale
  Intel_XeSS_3.0): "Overlay: installed true | presents 0 drawn 0". (tcB395's DLSS frame generation goes through
  Streamline: that one always worked.)
- Fix (layer, render/dx12_hook.cpp): the swap chain classes of libxess_fg.dll (XefgInterpolationSwapChain) and
  amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12.dll (FrameInterpolationSwapChainDX12Stable) are found by their RTTI names and
  get the same Present / Present1 / ResizeBuffers hooks (own originals; looked for again later, as the libraries
  load when the option is switched on; tiny "return 0" stubs are not hooked). tcB407 then faulted on the first
  frame ("exception 0xC0000005 ... stage 11": XeSS's proxy answers GetDevice(ID3D12CommandQueue) with S_OK and
  something that is not a queue); the queue is now asked for safely (IUnknown + QueryInterface under SEH) and the
  existing fallback (the present thread's ExecuteCommandLists) takes over. The render hook now says the exception
  code and a stage number when it disables itself.
- tcB409 (XeSS-FG, title): "Overlay ready: 4 buffers ... presents 16834 drawn 8416", the title menu on screen.
  tcB410 (AMD FSR Frame Generation selected, on this Nvidia card): its class hooked, the overlay draws.
  tcB411 (XeSS-FG, two first-time players, the whole flow into the world): both alive, overlay drawn on both, the
  pause menu's Co-op tab there, no "Overlay disabled", SAVES OK.
- tcB405 (new harness switch -PackageIni: both copies on the package's own coopplus.ini): the session works with the
  real defaults; nothing stuck on screen.

### 2026-11-11 14:20-14:50: AI control research (local notes build/decomp/notes_ai_control.md) and a first hand-over

- Read in code (research agent, static): the two messages do NOT hand control over. AiControlChangeCheatReq (2940,
  u32 actor key) only RESTARTS the AI of an NPC the requester already controls (AI session + 1 exe+0x2B64FD0, move
  session + 1 exe+0x2B66830, action reset exe+0x222C920, then ChangeAiControlAck 2660 to the near sessions); the
  client's 2660 handler (exe+0xC77370) acts only when its user key == client actor+0x90 (action reset, event
  "OnAi"), and acts on the PREVIOUS actor when the key is not loaded there (a trap, like 2985).
- The controller is written once, at creation (exe+0x29CCBB1): the spawner's user, else the owner, else the spawn
  request's user. Nothing re-assigns it. Every AI / movement request (MoveActorReq, StartAIFunctionReq, ...) is taken
  from the controller only, silently dropped otherwise.
- Client: actor+0x90 comes from the load record (first u32 of the actor body in ActorLoadDataAck 2005); the control
  mode byte actor+0xC8 is computed by exe+0x5AF410 (0 when the local user is not the controller); the AI task
  (exe+0x9A8000) runs only actors with a non-zero mode and re-checks only those, so taking control needs an explicit
  exe+0x5AF410 call.
- Server visibility: 64 m sectors (floor(pos / 64)), a user gets the 3x3 block around its character; RemoveActorAck
  3067 outside it. The agent GUESSED (80%) that this is the freeze: the host's client no longer has the bandits.
- MY CHECK OF THAT GUESS, before testing: by the sector numbers the shrine (-10344, -3992) = sector (-162, -63) and
  the dock bandits (-10241, -3956) = (-161, -62) are NEIGHBOURS, so the host should still have them; and in ff2 the
  host listed 144 NPC actors within 200 m. So "removed from the host's client" is doubtful; the cause may be a
  distance rule inside the client's AI steps after all, or the sector grid has another origin. NOT settled.
- Built (native, local, not committed yet): session2/ai_handoff.cpp, [session2] ai_handoff = 0 | probe | 1, default
  0. Host, server thread, once a second (trade entry 0xC0DE0008): an NPC with no owner whose controller's character is
  outside its 3x3 block while another player's is inside, twice in a row -> [actor+0x90] = that player's user key +
  the game's three restart steps; the new controller's client gets a private 12-byte 2660 (magic 0xC0DEA1C7 | key |
  new controller) that the receive hook turns into "client actor+0x90 = me, exe+0x5AF410(actor)" and drops, then
  the game's own 2660. A 2660 for a key that is not loaded is dropped (the trap). Plus a facts line every 10 s: the
  10 NPCs nearest to the other player with type, controller, distance to both players.
- ff4 (running): the lure test with ai_handoff=probe and the host listing its loaded NPCs 60-200 m away, to learn
  who controls the frozen bandits and whether the host's client still has them. The rule (sectors or plain
  distance) is decided from that.

### 2026-11-11 15:10-15:40: WHY a guest far from the host takes and deals no damage: the game's 80 m rule

- Research (local notes build/decomp/notes_hostility.md; read in code, the cause itself inferred until tested): the
  server has NO "are they enemies" test on a blow. A blow is accepted from the attacker's controller (exe+0x2BE1C10
  -> .tls$ 0xE31F4E0), its damage is a Damage buff (0x2B11EB0 -> 0x2E929A0 -> ServerDamageBuffProcessor ->
  0x225AD70 -> 0x225C8E0), and in 0x225C8E0 (asm 0x225CD3E..0x225D08C) THE AMOUNT IS SET TO 0 WHEN THE VICTIM IS
  80 m OR MORE HORIZONTALLY (30 m vertically; 500 m with the GlobalDetectTarget buff) FROM THE CHARACTER OF THE USER
  WHO OWNS THE VICTIM'S FIELD. Switch byte [exe+0x71436A8] (1), limits float [exe+0x7143798] = 80.0 and
  [exe+0x71437E8] = 30.0. For every victim, player or NPC.
- In the shared world both players are in the HOST's field. So more than 80 m from the host nothing can be hurt: the
  guest takes no damage there (ff3 / ff5 at 102-119 m) and its own blows do none (the playtest's "enemies do not
  react to the guest's attacks" may partly be this). This is the first explanation that fits every run of today.
  Not explained yet: ff5's 6 blows on the guest reported by the host's client "while both stood at the dock" (the
  distance per blow was not logged; a second gate, the faction test exe+0x1934E80, is the candidate if it shows
  again within 80 m).
- Relations, for the record: exe+0x23EA890(A, B, flag) = 0 enemy, 1 neutral, 2 ally, 4 cannot hurt; by FACTIONS per
  actor (info row +0x1A8, override u16 [[status+0x428]], extra list status+0xC0), not by a per-user enemy list;
  "you attacked me" = the NPC's aggro list ([[npc+0x68]+0x90] +0x108), written only by its controller's client.
  The client AI picks targets among every nearby actor by that relation (no "my own character only" test found).
- Checked by disassembly (new tool tools/disasm_rva.py, capstone on the archived exe): at exe+0x225D011 the victim's
  position is in xmm6 / xmm9 / xmm10 (x, z, y), the field owner's in xmm11 / xmm12 / xmm13, the limits in xmm0 /
  xmm1, the two actors' sizes in xmm8 / xmm7.
- Built (native, local): session2/damage_range.cpp, [session2] damage_range_players (default 1), host only: a
  mid-function hook at exe+0x225D011 (bytes checked first): when the field owner's character is out of range of the
  victim but another player's character is in range, that player's position stands in for the owner's in this one
  comparison. Far from every player the game's rule still holds (far NPC fights stay harmless). Player positions
  come from the once-a-second server check (also used by ai_handoff). Log: "DamageRange ON ...", "a hit N m from the
  field owner's character counts ...", a counts line once a minute.
- To test next (ff6 / ff7): the lure scene at 108 m with the hook: does the guest lose HP (with ai_handoff=1, so the
  bandits go for it), and do the guest's own blows there take HP off a bandit (the npcs step shows HP).

### 2026-11-11 15:50-16:05: two side effects found by reading my own new code and the logs (fixed in source)

- (1) The mod's own once-a-second request to its server-thread entry (trade 3111 with entry 0xC0DE0008, needed by
  the damage range fix; entry 7 for chest shares before) wrote TWO log lines per second into the host's cdmp.log
  ("Inject C>S: opcode 3111 ... posted", "TradeProbe [handler] 3111 reached the server's handler"): ff7 had 654 such
  lines in 9 minutes. Now the first 10 / 16 are logged, then every 1000th (failures always). Native, local.
- (2) PACKET RECORDING IN SOLO. The base's sniffer default is [sniffer] record=1: every packet goes to
  bin64\cdmp_packets_<date>.log / .bin, no size limit (the base's own note: 310 MB in 16 minutes). The co-op ini the
  layer writes has had record=0 since 2026-11-09, but the SOLO ini (also the cdmp.ini shipped in every package)
  had no [sniffer] section. So a player with the mod installed who sits at the title or plays solo records
  everything. Seen in the real-install log of pp2: "Sniffer v2 ... writing cdmp_packets_<date-time>.log/.bin",
  "recording through a disk queue". This is in every posted shared-world build, including 3c46bec5. It may be part
  of the low frame rate a tester reported; not measured.
  Fixed three ways: the solo ini text gets "[sniffer] record=0" (layer, net/native_mode_text.h, unit test), the
  package script writes the same into the shipped cdmp.ini, and the base's own default is now record=0 (native,
  local). The harness's own test inis still say record=1 for the minute before the lobby restart; to be set to 0.
- How found: not by a test. I measured which log lines a normal session writes most, then looked at the size of
  the logs in the game folder. Neither is in the checklist yet: a "disk and log growth" check is added next (size
  of everything the session wrote into bin64, lines per minute).

### t5, lt1, t6, t7 (2026-11-11 17:46-18:30): the guest joins at the host's side; what a body's loot really is

- JOIN (t5-lowsave, layer build of 17:40 with [coop] join_beside_host, default 1): guest log "Co-op: joined: our
  save's place was 1321 m from the host: moved to its side (-10349, -3920)"; it ends 1 m from the host; screenshot
  t5-lowsave-g0 shows both at Nas River, the host's name plate and the Interact prompt, the guest's own prologue
  quest still tracked ("Return to your comrades"). A guest whose save is already beside the host is left alone
  ("already 1 m from the host, not moved", t5-loot). Tested: one PC, a guest on a 1-mission save, host on its usual
  save. NOT tested: a guest who is in a cutscene or on a mount when the 4 s are over, a guest in another region
  with a loading screen between, two PCs.
- BODY LOOT (four runs, probe on in lt1 and t7): a loot request for a body (LootingDropFromDeadBodyReq 2491, the
  same request the old test cheat sent) is answered "err 0" every time, but most requests take NOTHING: the probe
  shows the body's pool unchanged ("pool 4 -> 4") in 9 of 12 requests and one item taken in 3 ("pool 4 -> 3"). The
  friend's share is made from what the looter's bag gained, so there is a share only for those. t5: 0 of 2, t6: 0 of
  6 (hence its FAIL), t7: 1 of 6, lt1: 1 of 2; each share reached the guest ("is there and got its own share ...
  its bag gained 1 piece(s)"). It was never the package's settings (the native ini files of a failing and a passing
  run are byte-identical, the layer's Config lines too): my suspicion of that in between was wrong.
- OPEN QUESTION this raises (not answered): in tcB387 this morning single requests took 4 kinds at once (x2, x5, x9,
  x7). Why a request takes everything there and nothing here is not understood (kill by a blow against KillCheat at
  full health? the quest's state?). And how a real player's loot key maps to these requests (one request per item, or
  one for all) is unchecked. If a player's own looting takes its items LATER than 1.5 s after the request, the
  friend's share would be missed: to check with the probe on while looting by hand, or by two players. Until then
  "enemy loot for both" is: works when the request itself takes items; unverified for hand looting.
- The checklist's loot step now kills ten bandits and asks each body twice, with the probe on, and says plainly when
  no request took anything (then the step is run again; it says nothing about the share).
- Layer dev steps (dev only): killnear [radius], lootlast. Switches: build/native/t5-*.args, lt1.args, t6-*.args,
  t7.args.
- ANSWERED from the earlier research notes (build/decomp/notes_lootr_bodies_chests.md A.1 / A.2, read in code on
  2026-11-10; I should have read them before writing "open question"): the natural loot (the interaction on a body,
  its loot buff and timer 2026) and the 2491 request call the SAME worker, and one hook at its entry covers all four
  call sites. A take is always "every pool entry of kind 0", moved into the looter's bag in ONE bag transaction at
  that moment (there is no loot window). So hand looting gives the friend its share exactly like the request does,
  and 1.5 s is not a race. "pool 4 -> 4" means the body had no kind-0 entry: its drops were of the other kinds (kind
  3 = thrown on the ground by the death event, kinds 6 / 9 special), which never go through the worker. tcB387's big
  takes were bodies with kind-0 entries. What stays unverified is only what a second player sees on screen.

### nc5 (2026-11-11 20:50) and mr1 (21:05): New Co-op Save: THE GUEST NEVER GETS IN (found, cause read, fix built)

- nc5 (the harness scrolls and accepts the agreement for the host in the test copy, Space on the difficulty): the
  HOST starts the story: "Unfamiliar Lands / Return to your comrades", Day 0, Hills of No Return, at night
  (nc5-h0). The GUEST stays on "Waiting for Host / Joining the start of the story..." until the run ends, 13 minutes.
- Cause, from the logs and the game's code (read today, exe+0x2EBBAF0 = the user login):
  - guest log: "out LoginCharacterToFieldServerReq 2733 ... save slot 103"; host log: "C2 identity: refused user 2's
    Req 2733: user 2's lobby does not hold 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFF002"; the host's status line shows "blocked 1" from then on.
  - a normal run has, at the guest's login, "LoadSlot ... from exe+0x2EBBE90 ... user 2 | slot 103 -> REMAP 204",
    "the staged guest slot moved in", "user 2's lobby loads from slot204", "C2 identity: user 2 lobby ... written".
    nc5 has none of them: "slot 204 staged | LoadSlot calls 0 ... moved in 0" every minute.
  - the user login re-reads the save folder, takes the save manager's latest slot and loads the lobby from it ONLY
    if a slot is there. A brand-new co-op world has no slot until the host's new game writes one, and the guest
    logs in three minutes before that. No lobby load -> the guest's uploaded save is never moved in -> user 2 has
    no character -> its character login is refused -> the client waits for ever.
  - So "New Co-op Save" cannot work for any pair on the shared-world base as posted. It was last tested on the old
    base (2026-11-06); on the shared world the harness always took "Continue Our Co-op Save" (see 19:55).
- Fix (native, local): when the guest's upload is staged and the co-op world's account folder has no slot folder at
  all, the staged slot is moved in at once (guest_save_host.cpp), so the login's re-read finds a slot and the usual
  remap loads user 2's lobby from it. nc6 runs it.
- Also in nc5's log: the guest's staged save came "from mailbox gen15" (its newer progress kept on the host from
  earlier sessions) instead of the upload: by design a guest brings its own save into any world, a new one too.
  For two real new players both saves are new. Whether "New Co-op Save" should give a returning guest a NEW
  character is a design question for the owner (the card says "Both of you begin the story"): queued.
- mr1 (mounts, first try): no horse came for either player. The harness called it with the keyboard wheel (hold F1,
  cursor on a slot), which was written for an older game build; the horse is called with D-pad Up held and the
  right stick pushed down (memory: horse-call-method), and the simulated pad had no sticks. Added (layer, dev only):
  in a simulated press 0x0400 = right stick down, 0x0800 = left stick up; "pad 0401 2500" = the horse call.
  Script scan/mount_call.txt. Next: mr2 with -HostDev pad_sim=1 -GuestDev pad_sim=1.

### of1 / of2 (2026-11-11 23:24-23:42): the far-fight fix was HALF WRONG; corrected (native 19be296)

- Runs: the host draws its dock bandits for 26 s, then goes 484 m away (Hernand); the guest stays and swings for a

- Both runs: the bandits DO attack the guest that far from the host (blows reported by the guest's client:
  of1 "guest>NPC 61 ... NPC>guest 53", of2 "guest>NPC 67 ... NPC>guest 37"), so nobody is frozen at 484 m, with or
  without the hand-off. But the guest's health never left 300/300, and the host's hook line said "field owner out
  of range 103 | counted because another player was in range 0" (of2: 129 / 0). In the farfight step (108 m) the
  same line reads 28 / 28. (The four "kills" the tally shows are from before the host left.)
- Cause, from the game's code again (asm exe+0x225CE7A..0x225CF30): at the hook the VICTIM is x xmm11, z xmm9,
  y xmm10 and the field owner's character is x xmm6, z xmm12, y xmm13. My hook paired (6, 9, 10) as the victim and
  (11, 12, 13) as the owner: a point made of the owner's x and the victim's z. With that, "is a player near the
  victim" was in effect "is the victim within 80 m of the HOST along z", and the replacement left the game
  comparing only that z difference. At the dock / shrine pair the host stood 36 m away along z (the old log even
  said so: "another player is 37 m from the victim", for a guest standing 2 m from its victim), so ff7, pp5 and
  pp6's farfight passed. 256 m away along z nothing counted.
- Fixed: the right registers for both the test and the replacement. Built with the no-save-guest change as package
  d5c06748; of3 (the same run as of1) is the check: the hook line must count hits and the guest must lose health.
- What this changes: the changelog's far-fight line was true only for that geometry. Builds 980c5b38 and 2ddd622f
  are not candidates any more (waiting list corrected). The farfight checklist step gets a second geometry (the
  host far along the other axis) so the same mistake cannot pass again.
- ai_handoff: of2 handed 64 NPCs to the guest's user ("handed over 64 ... noted 64") and nothing broke, but
  of1 shows the enemies act without it. Still no evidence that it is needed; stays off.

  swap chain in its own class only when one of its plugins needs it; on this Nvidia PC it always does, so the hook
  on its class has always worked here. On his AMD card it evidently does not, and the game presents through
  DXGI's own class. Our "no Streamline" path would have hooked that one, but Streamline IS loaded there. NOT
  VERIFIED on AMD hardware (there is none here).

  unhooked, no fallback = his state): "presents 0 drawn 0" all session, and the guest STILL got into the world
  here (the mod's E press took, in the world 44 s later). So "never left the title" is not a consequence of the
  missing overlay on this PC. What differs on his: unknown. Candidates: his game was not the window in front (the
  mod waits up to 3 min for that, and says so only on the screen he could not see), or he had opened one of the

    direct queue, hooked at install now) and for 4 s no Present comes through a hooked class -> the class a NEW
    swap chain gets on this PC is hooked too (found with a throwaway 64x64 swap chain, the old "no Streamline"
    way). On a PC where frames do come through a hooked class this never runs, so the old crash (DLSS frame
    generation picking the throwaway up, 1 launch in 5) is not brought back for those PCs.
  - A second trigger with the 5 s status line (8 s without a frame, 20 s where DLSS-G's plugin is loaded, the game's
    window in front) for a PC where the command queue hook sees nothing.
  - "No frame" means none for that long, not none ever: switching frame generation off in the settings mid-session
    (from the library's class to DXGI's own) is covered. The late hook stays out of the way when a class above it
    presents (2 s rule, and the existing same-thread rule).

  (the window is rarely in front at the 5 s check). It also showed: on THIS PC the throwaway's class is

  throwaway gives "the class a swap chain gets on this PC", which is what the game got; and this PC can only test

### Checklist pp8 on 0.1.0-alpha+47135b83, steps 1-10 (2026-11-12 04:58-06:00): 304 PASS, 2 FAIL, neither in the package

- static FAIL "layer / kit / tools have uncommitted changes": tools/gen/progress_chart.py (the chart script, edited
  for the next chart, not part of the package). Committed (5452cee). The package is unchanged: it is still built
  from 47135b8 / native 6f0c5ef, and static compares the package's two .asi with the build output by hash.
- fsr FAIL "guest: native log: 1 unknown error line": `GuestS3 first-chance AV at 0x13FFE0196 kind 0x8 addr
  0x13FFE0196` at 05:20:10.946, 2 ms after RemoteMotion wrote its inline hook (05:20:10.944), on another thread.
  The game went on (the guest played to the end of the step, every other check passed).
  WHAT IT IS (read in the hook library's source, safetyhook os.windows.cpp trap_threads / trap_handler): while a
  hook is written, the library makes the page it patches AND the page of the trampoline ('to') read/write, i.e.
  not executable, and its exception handler lets a thread that faults in either page retry until the protection
  is back (find_trap_page -> EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION). 0x13FFE0000 / 0x13FFF0000 are the two 64 KB regions
  right below the exe where the trampolines live (the base's HookPrepare line lists them). So a thread that was
  running an EARLIER hook's trampoline at that instant faults once, is retried, and the base's first-chance
  logger writes an ERR line before the library's handler takes it. The same event as the long-known
  "AV at 0x7FF... kind 0x8" (a system DLL's page), only in the trampoline page.
  HOW OFTEN: 10 logs since tc29 (2026-11-06): tc29, tcB107, tcB117, tcB148, tcB162, tcB220, tcB303, tcB309, tcB331,
  pp8-fsr; the 0x7FF form in 66 logs. The game went on in all of them.
  The checklist knew only the 0x7FF form. FIX IN THE CHECKER (tools/prepost.sh, 5452cee): the known pattern is now
  `AV at 0x(7FF|13FF[EF])... kind 0x8`. Not a change to the package.
  LATER (base, next build): the first-chance logger should not write these as ERR at all (ask the hook library
  whether the address is in a page it is patching); a tester's report then has no false alarm in it either.
- Both steps are run again as "pp8b" (static, fsr) before steps 11-19, the other eight steps of the first half stand:
  the checker change can only turn that one line from FAIL to PASS. Re-running `static` under pp8 would have
  emptied the result file (it starts it).
- Looked at: pp8-latehook-Wguest05 / Wguest10 (the waiting screen IS drawn on the guest with Streamline's class
  unhooked), -L1-host-start-coop (the menu, the party list, Start Co-op lit), -39-guest-view (both in the world);
  pp8-display-01 (the title menu on the real display mode); pp8-real-02; revive g1/g2 (the death screen with Q / U),
  g4 (up again); chest (both at the shrine); fsr / xess 39 views. SAVES OK and "user install restored: 5/5 OK" in
  all nine game steps (real: REAL SAVES UNCHANGED).
- latehook numbers: 4.35 s from "game is up" to the late hook on the host's co-op launch.

### rt1a (2026-11-12 08:07-08:26): a second Start Co-op restarts both games, and then the HOST'S TUNNEL IS DEAD

- Next-build code (layer: a second Start Co-op in a launch that already ran one restarts both games; a guest that is
  not let in says so; native: the trapped-thread line as INF) built at 08:05. Test rt1a (scratchpad explore7.sh rt1:
  `-HostDev lobby_retry=1`, the host's first automatic start is a second Start Co-op instead).
- The layer part works as written: host 08:08:26 "[dev] lobby_retry: instead of starting, a second Start Co-op:
  both games restart again"; the guest (already a guest) 08:08:26 "the host restarts into co-op; we follow when it
  is back", 08:08:47 "the host is back in co-op: this game restarts as its guest"; 08:09:07 host "both games are in
  co-op: starting your co-op save".
- Then nobody got into the world (240 s each). Host's base, 08:08:54.710: `ERR Session2: the Troc tunnel stops: the
  link broke (reconnection or overflow); session 2's conversation is lost until the game restarts`. Guest's base to
  the end: "host ready no", tunnel "out 0 packets, in 0 packets".
- Cause: common/troc_link.cpp marks the link broken on ANY second connection (`epoch_ != 0 || ...`), and the host's
  tunnel_tick (session2.cpp) kills the tunnel for the whole launch when the link is broken. At a FIRST start the
  guest's old process is in solo mode and never is on the host's tunnel. At a SECOND start the guest's old process is
  already in guest mode: it is on the new host's tunnel for the 2 s before it restarts (the host's tunnel opened
  08:08:46.8, the old guest left 08:08:49, the new one connected 08:08:54) and its successor counts as a
  reconnection. Nothing had gone either way on that first connection (out 0, in 0).
- So "a second Start Co-op restarts both games" could NEVER have worked without a change in the base. The same holds
  for any guest that restarts its game while the host waits at the title in co-op mode (a crash of the guest's game
  before the start, for one): the host's tunnel was dead until the host restarted too.
- Fix (native, session2.cpp tunnel_tick, not the reconnect mode): a broken link with packets_in 0, packets_out 0, no
  held Req and no user 2 is reset (WRN "the guest's connection was replaced by a new one before anything was said on
  it"); anything else kills the tunnel as before. The counters are cumulative for the process (TunnelSender::reset
  keeps packets_sent), so "nothing was ever said" is exact. Test rt1b.
- The harness is not at fault here: it waited for "-> REMOTE" in the guest's log (420 s), which never came.
- SAVES OK, user install restored: 5/5 OK.

     the mark, so for a host that had loaded ANY world in this launch the NativeRestart phase was reset one tick
     after it began. Fixed: host_restart_into sets g_gen_mark.

     written): a host who has loaded a world in this game session (played solo, went back to the title, then
     invited a friend) presses Start Co-op, picks a save, and nothing happens; the friend's game says "Waiting
     for Host" for ever. Shown by rt3a for a host that came back from its CO-OP world; for the solo case it is
     read from the code only (the counter is the layer's character capture, the same in solo). NOT tested with a
     solo load: in the harness a solo-mode copy would load the owner's REAL save (no redirect in solo mode), so
     that test is not run. Workaround for players: restart the game before Start Co-op.
  2. The goodbye did not reach the guest at the title (the activity channel; no "the host is ending the session"
     in its log). Now the lobby channel carries it: kMsgSessionEnded (25), sent by lobby_session_ended on the
     host; a guest at the title goes back to its menu and STAYS IN THE PARTY; a guest in the world ignores it (the

### The host's reload crash explained (research 2026-11-12 ~12:15; local notes build/decomp/notes_host_reload_crash.md)

- CORRECTION of two earlier notes (tcB291 on 2026-11-10 and the tester report above): it is NOT "a request of the
  guest handled while the host's world unloads". With the posted build's symbols the base's frame is troc_detour's
  branch for a subject that is not user 2, and the "stack" of our crash line is a scan of the stack, not a call
  chain (two of its entries are vtables, one is the Troc object itself).
- What runs: ExecuteTroc (exe+0x29AD450) of opcode 2049, TrUpdateScheduleStageOnceTimer: a SERVER TIMER, not a
  request of either client. Its handler (exe+0xE691180) takes its subject's field, calls the field's vtable +0x48
  (ServerField 0x2D984B0: the field OWNER's sequencer stage manager) and reads [manager+0x170] with no null test:
  the crash at 0xE6911E5. The answer is 0 when the owner cannot be resolved ("valid logined" lookup fails) or has
  no manager. Which of the two at a reload: not determined.
- Why only with a guest (inferred): alone, the owner's unload detaches the field from every timer subject first and
  the handler's own "field not attached" exit catches it; with a guest the field stays attached while its owner is
  gone for a moment. 313 host reloads passed in the tester's session before one timer fell into the gap. The
  sibling timers 2047 and 2050 have the same unguarded read.
- Fix written (native, session2/user2_funnels.cpp, NOT built yet): before a 2047 / 2049 / 2050 runs, for any
  subject, the field is asked the same question (its vtable +0x48, under SEH); no manager = the timer is answered
  as the game answers "field not attached" (*res = 0) and not run. WRN line for the first 20, a count in the
  summary. Dev switch [session2] schedule_timer_guard_test=N: N timers are skipped although the owner is there
  (does a skipped tick break the NPC schedules? the research could not say; a skipped call would have decremented
  a counter in the schedule object).
- Not covered by the fix: an owner torn down on ANOTHER thread between our question and the handler's (in the
  report the unload ran on the same thread as the crash, so not expected).
- To test: (1) schedule_timer_guard_test with two players: schedules go on; (2) the host reloads its world with the
  guest next to it, many times (the checkpoint revive U moves and reloads): no crash, and whether the guard's count
  ever rises on this PC.

### The fresh save for the friend on a New Co-op Save: how the guest's save works today, and the design (read of the base's code, 2026-11-12 ~12:30; nothing built)

How it works today (file references in the research's report; S2 = cdmp-native/src/mod/session2):
- The guest offers the newest save.save under ITS redirected save root. On a real install that root is
  `coop_worlds\guest_of_<host>`, seeded "keep": a ONE-TIME copy of the guest's real saves made at the first join with
  that host. So the offer is a frozen solo snapshot (D3vils' 1,858-mission character).
- The host stages the upload as its world's slot 204 and user 2 plays it. If the upload is the root of a "line" in
  the host's mailbox (%LOCALAPPDATA%\cdmp\guest_saves\<guest id>\gen<n>, 5 kept) and a newer generation exists, the
  host stages THAT instead: the only way co-op progress comes back today. The guest's co-op character therefore
  already lives on the HOST's PC, keyed by guest id and line root, NOT by world: that is why a returning guest
  arrives in a brand-new world with the old character.
- Results sent back to the guest land in %LOCALAPPDATA%\cdmp\guest_progress\<host>\incoming and nothing applies
  them.
- No code makes or recognises an empty save. A new co-op world is the real save folder copied without its slot
  folders; the host's New Game then autosaves slot0 at world entry (nc7: "slot 0 -> REMAP 204", Day 0).
Design chosen (A, host-authoritative, with a world marker):
- `<world>\cdmp_coop_world.txt` written as `user2_character=pending` when a world is made with seed "new". Worlds
  made by copy (Start From My Solo Progress) and old worlds have none and behave as today.
- In a marker world the guest's upload is verified and acknowledged but never staged. At user 2's login gate (the
  2535 hold of e3583a7) the host stages, in this order: pending -> a copy of the host's own first complete slot
  (both at mission 0), marker rewritten with the guest id and the line root; later sessions -> the newest mailbox
  generation of that root; else `<world>_guest_prev\...\slot204`; else re-seed from the host's newest slot (WRN).
- So the run's character for the friend is named by the line root in the world's marker and lives on the host's PC.
  The friend's solo saves are never used for that world; a different partner's world has its own marker.
- Rejected: B (the guest's game makes its own new game first: agreement, difficulty, opening, a restart, all by
  keys); C (ship a template save: none exists).
- Files: S2/save_hooks.cpp (marker at a "new" seed; `_guest_prev` moved with a world set aside), a new pure
  S2/coop_world_logic.h (marker text, slot picker, staging order), S2/guest_save_host.cpp/.h, S2/guest_save_tunnel.cpp
  (finish_upload; the gate's staging), S2/server.cpp (the gate), config ([session2] coop_world_character=1|0), unit
  tests; layer: card wording only; harness: back up the marker and `_guest_prev` with the test world.
- Risks named by the research, to be settled by tests: does the host's first autosave replay the opening for user 2;
  identical item numbers on both (as the old clone mode, which ran for hours); the first slot may still be
  `slot0_new` when the gate looks; the mailbox keeps 5 generations across all lines; a guest with no local save
  still cannot press Play; the label's base must be the root.
- Tests planned: newsave with another guest save (the guest at mission 0 on its screen, "seeded from the host's
  slot"), Continue of that world (the guest where it left), the same with the mailbox emptied, the old world on
  Continue (unchanged), solostart after a marker world, a guest with no save.

### 2026-11-12 12:15-12:30, while pp9's first ten steps run (no builds): travel research, the fresh save written, a Steam fault in pp9-display

- TRAVEL (research, local notes build/decomp/notes_far_teleport.md; nothing run):
  - Why DoTeleportAck 3052 stops at about 50 m: the client's handler asks its navigation data for a standable cell at
    the target, and the target's 32 m nav chunk must be within 2 chunks of the client's nav window. Far targets have
    no nav data on the client. Not a constant to change. 3052 is the game's blink for AI companions, not a player
    move; its 8 trailing bytes are a session id that is echoed back, no flag.
  - How the game moves a player far: a PENDING RELOAD. The server stores a destination on the character's transform
    component and the client's loading machine sends GameLoadingStartReq 2294 by itself; the server then applies it.
    Fast travel is ReloadStageStartReq 3074 (53 bytes: u32 0 | u32 FieldInfoKey | u32 actor | vec3 pos | quat | vec3
    scale | u8 flag); with actor = 0 the packet's position is taken with NO waypoint, unlock, distance or cheat
    test. TeleportRevivePointAck 3071 (u32 actor | u32 art) only starts the client's loading screen. The teleport
    item does exactly "destination + 3071".
  - Recommended (confirmed statically, never run): as player X inject Req 3074 `0 | X's FieldInfoKey | 0 | P | quat |
    (1,1,1) | 1`, at once send Ack 3071 `K | 0` to X's client; the client loads and sends 2294 itself. For user 2
    the base's fast-travel funnel must be live (it is in the package: user2_fast_travel=1). The tcB16 trial of
    2026-11-07 sent actor = the host's key, which the worker refuses for a remote player: it most likely never set
    a destination. The cheat teleports (2917, 2126) are stripped in the retail exe.
  - To build: "Go to my friend" and the join beside the host through this (a loading screen, then there), hops only
    for the last metres or as the fallback.
- THE FRESH SAVE: written in the base by an implementation pass, NOT compiled (uncommitted in upstream/cdmp-native:
  session2/coop_world_logic.h new; save_hooks, guest_save_host, guest_save_tunnel, server.cpp, config, mod.cpp,
  tests). Its own list of doubts: the pending seed takes the host's most recent complete slot; reading the host's
  slot can collide with a host save for a few ms; after a fallback `_guest_prev` could hold the friend's solo
  character and be adopted; no lock on the gate's state (it assumes the gate and the tunnel run on the network
  thread). To compile, review and test (ten scenarios listed in its report).
- pp9-display FAILED two checks (the package dc7ade5e, a REAL Steam launch): `Crash log: exception 0xC0000005 at

## Shared cutscenes: the owner's design pick (2026-11-13 ~17:00): the READY CHECK

- Asked with three options (watch along / ready check / own story each); the owner picked "Ready check first" (Jay's idea): a story trigger waits until both players are there and both press interact, then each game plays the scene. Memory: cutscene-ready-check.
- What it needs: (1) knowing a story trigger when the host's client meets one (its Req: interaction, SequencerTriggerVolumeInOutReq 2808, a quest step), (2) holding it until the joined player is there and has pressed too, (3) the scene playing in the joined player's game as well (the base's guest_seq_play never played one: 43 created, 0 played; not ported), (4) what the scene brings into the world (a story boss) visible to both.
- Measurement first, on a New Co-op Save (both start ~50 m from the first objective "Return to your comrades"): scratchpad cs.sh <name> host|guest|both (backs up and puts back the test co-op world). cs1 = the host walks there, the guest stays.
- Note: the layer's prologue_hold says "while either player is in the prologue, co-op works as if far apart: no shared cutscenes / skip vote"; a New Co-op Save is at 0 missions: to check what that switch does in the shared world.
- cs1 / cs2 (New Co-op Save, the host walks ~45 m toward "Return to your comrades"; cs2 with [dev] native_record=1, the new layer switch that writes [sniffer] record=1 into both native inis; recordings moved to build/native/captures/cs2):
  - THE TRIGGER: at the cabin the host's client sends SequencerTriggerVolumeInOutReq (2808) `BC 01 00 00 | 00 00 00 00 | 03 00 00 20 | 01 00 10 A0 | 00` = sequencer 0x1BC, kind 0x20000003, the host's own character 0xA0100001; at once StageBranchStateReq 0x1BC; the server answers StageOnBranchEventAck, UpdateMissionUIStateListAck, DeleteSequencerAck 0x1BC, UpdateStageListAck, UpdateMissionListAck (the quest steps on). 0.6 s later the host's client starts its cutscene (layer "Activity: our cutscene started"; 33 s). The cutscene itself runs in the host's client; the server sees only the trigger and the mission update. The other 2808s name NPC gimmicks (0xB...) with kinds 0x20000006 / 0x20000022.
  - The guest's base received the host's scene messages (GuestSeqRoute routed 23-24 "foreign" 2661s into X) and played none (as known).
  - Time base for the recordings: "capture t=" in the host's ObserverStage lines = the .log's t (cs2: t 496.80 = 17:46:42.96).
  - Side facts: the host's and the guest's clocks differ on a New Co-op Save (host "Day 0 Sun 10:45 PM", guest "Day 1 Mon 1:00 AM"); the guest's own opening cutscene played when it joined (17:26:33-17:27:11).
- Next: cs3, the GUEST walks there alone (does its client send the 2808 for its own character, and does the server run the stage for user 2?).
- cs3 (the GUEST walks the same ~35 m past the trigger spot, recording on): the guest's client sent NO SequencerTriggerVolumeInOutReq at all (0 of 17 395 Reqs), no StageBranchStateReq, no UpdateStageChartEventReq; no scene of its own started. Its packets: PrepareSequencerAck x44, ALL for the host's character 0xA0100001 (the base's copies, routed into X, never played); UpdateStageListAck x79 for its OWN character 0xA0100116 (its stage list exists); UpdateMissionListAck x37 host's + x6 its own.
  => THE FOUNDATIONAL GAP: the host's server prepares story sequencers (2661) only for the host's character. The host got 22 of them at world entry (t 198.6, with no Req of its client before them: the server does it by itself when the character enters). For user 2's character none, so the guest's client has no stage sequencers, so no trigger volumes, so no story scenes of its own. A ready check needs this first: the server must prepare user 2's own stage sequencers (as for the host), then both clients have the trigger and the gate can hold both 2808s.
  - Not the User2Stages D/S/F refusals: those are NPC schedule hooks (2976-era checksums, refused since the base).

- 16:50 mudai's "locked into the radmin co-op session until I uninstalled the mod" / "the game won't even start up"
  (#general 16:20-16:34 UTC), from the code, no logs yet: a co-op launch is set in the native base's mode file and
  the layer puts the next launch back to Solo in lobby_native_init (coop_lobby.cpp: no fresh restart marker ->
  Solo). That runs only when `kNativeLayer && in_game && build_ok && cfg.coop_enabled` (mod.cpp:2299). So a player
  who switches Co-op+ off (or a game build the layer refuses) keeps the native base starting in the last co-op role
  (Host / Guest, direct address) on EVERY launch; nothing else resets it, and uninstalling removes the mode file.
  A likely way to "locked in". Fix idea (not built yet): do the stale-mode reset whatever coop_enabled / build_ok
  say (it only touches our own mode file). Their report zip would confirm it; asking them needs the owner's OK.
